chapter: Family and growing up in Manhattan
title: Violin lessons and a musical family
summary: Procope was the youngest of three brothers; his father studied violin, his mother played piano and sang. He started violin at six and recalls being moved by his parents' music as a toddler.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And I just want you to tell me about how you started out. I know your brother Bill played several instruments and your parents also played, right? Tell me about it. Was it an older brother?

Yes, I was the youngest of three brothers in my family. I had one sister. She was -- she's the youngest, but I was the youngest brother, and we all played, you know, as children. We took music, you know, not intending to be professional musicians, but it was just part of our education. My father studied violin but never played anyplace. He just studied and studied and played at home. And my mother, who played piano and sang in the church choir, and that's how it all began. My brother and I, we started when we were six years old, with the violin. We took violin lessons. We started out and it's a funny thing, I took to it. When I first got a violin in my hands it was just like it was something I really liked. You know, with no thought of being a professional musician at all. I just liked it and I loved it, because, you know, well, I just loved it. It did a lot of things for me.

And before that I remember as far back as, I think -- as I always say, I remember when I was three years old, three and a half years old, four years old. We lived in Long Island, and you know, we used to have a big, large dining room. We had a fireplace and everything, you know. My father would come home in the evening, and after dinner my mother would play the piano and he'd play the violin and there's one incident that my mother always talked about. They were playing something on the piano. I don't know what it was. They used to play things like, "Poet and Peasant", and that sort of thing, and whatever they were playing, it just got to me, you know, and I just ran and jumped up on her lap and, you know, just like I was -- you know, like the music just --

Possessed, I suppose, yeah. It just moved me like that, you know. And all through my life, you know, right now, you know, I'll hear something and it just moves me, just music. Just music. It doesn't have to be jazz or anything in particular, just music. Yeah.
